headline: Senior Vice President, Mid-Corporate Relationship Manager | Citi | Connecting Global Business & Professional Service Corporations with Exceptional Domestic & Multinational Banking Solutions

location.linkedinText: Washington, District of Columbia, United States

topSkills: Treasury Management • Cross-border Transactions • Credit Structuring • Investment Banking • Corporate Finance
about:
From growing up in the Washington, D.C. area, to working in New York City, I have always had an affinity for connecting with business leaders. Surrounded by a diverse family of entrepreneurs, I have been inspired by the drive and passion of founders. Naturally, I have focused my career on connecting global organizations with solutions and services to help their businesses thrive.

As a Senior Vice President and Relationship Manager at Citi, I lead a team of specialists focused on understanding each client’s unique needs to deliver strategic financial guidance and comprehensive solutions. My mission is to help multinational corporations across the business and professional services industry thrive by achieving their business goals. I am responsible for cultivating new clients with annual revenues between $100MM and $15B, as well as managing a diverse portfolio of existing Corporate Bank relationships. Currently hold FINRA licenses: Securities Industry Essentials (SIE), Series 79, & Series 63.

Originally from Potomac, Maryland, I lived and worked in NYC for 15 years; graduated with a MBA from Fordham University, as well as a BS from Fordham, with concentrations in International Business, Finance and Spanish. I have a passion for learning about new cultures, studied in Argentina, and traveled to over 45 countries throughout my life. Aside from work and travel, I enjoy biking, hiking, skiing, and boating with family and friends.

If you would like to learn more about Citi’s Commercial & Investment Banking solutions, supporting global Business & Professional Service companies, then I would love to hear from you. Feel free to contact me via InMail.

Industry specialties: accounting, consulting, engineering, architecture, legal, government contracting, IT services, insurance, administrators, hospitality, travel, logistics, event management, project management, comercial and residential real estate, human resources, payroll, training, staffing, and equipment services.

headline: Strategic Data Manager | Social Entrepreneur | Charity Fundraiser | Marathon Enthusiast.
topSkills: Data Management • Financial Analysis • Management • Banking • Finance
about:
As a Strategic Data Management leader with over two decades of experience in enterprise data execution, compliance and cross‑functional leadership, I specialize in transforming complex data challenges into strategic opportunities that drive measurable impact. My career in risk and data management has honed my ability to align analytics with mission‑driven objectives and steward diverse teams toward success.

Beyond the corporate world, I am widely recognized as the Toghu Marathoner. I’ve completed 19 marathons across six continents in traditional Cameroonian Toghu attire, earning a Guinness World Record for the fastest marathon in Toghu and finishing all six Abbott World Marathon Majors. Each race is a platform to fundraise and advocate for causes close to my heart, including autism research, literacy programs, Ebola relief, and community infrastructure, impacting over 20,000 children.

As Founder and Managing Director of the Amom Foundation, I lead a mission to bridge educational gaps and support neurodiverse learners—especially those with autism. Our inclusive learning programs implement Teaching at the Right Level and autism-friendly approaches, while our grants, scholarships, teacher & parent training, and advocacy efforts champion inclusive education. Through these initiatives, we are building a school for children with autism and special needs in Cameroon.

Whether guiding organizations through data‑driven transformation, running marathons to raise awareness and funds, or advocating for inclusive education, I strive to be a champion for inclusion and opportunity in everything I do. I am currently spearheading the Yaoundé Cultural Marathon—a non‑competitive cultural race celebrating Cameroon’s heritage through traditional attire, cultural displays, live music, and community impact. Join me as we lace up to run for culture.

profileTopEducation.schoolName: Harvard University Kennedy School of Government

experience.description:
Founded Toghu Marathoner, a movement blending endurance running and cultural heritage to raise funds and awareness for causes including education, autism, and youth empowerment.

Organized and executed fundraising marathons across six continents, raising over US$180,000 for charitable projects in Cameroon and across Africa. 

Partnered with NGOs, cultural institutions, sponsors, and community leaders to build inclusive programs and advocacy (e.g. infrastructure, schooling, autism support).

Overseen coaching programs under “Toghu Marathoner” to mentor and transform aspiring runners (from beginners to marathon-ready), emphasizing purpose, resilience, and cultural identity.

Established Cameroon’s first cultural marathon festival, merging long-distance running with traditional music, dance, and attire to promote cultural tourism, national unity, and sports diplomacy.

Designed and launched the event framework in collaboration with ministries, the Cameroon Athletics Federation, and international cultural stakeholders.

Leading fundraising and sponsorship efforts targeting local and global partners to position Yaoundé as a sports tourism hub in Central Africa.

Driving event logistics, route planning, and festival integration for a 2026 debut expected to attract 10,000+ participants and international visitors.

Advocating inclusive participation, ensuring accessibility for neurodiverse and underrepresented communities through linked programs under the Amom Foundation.

about:
I turn strategy into execution, through a career focused on delivering strategic initiatives that translate into measurable client outcomes.

At Citi Commercial Bank (CCB), I lead the Global Business Execution team, which supports three global leaders – CCB CEO, CAO and Global Head of Coverage. My team’s mandate spans three pillars:
1.	Driving execution of CCB’s global strategic priorities.
2.	Managing core business operations.
3.	Serving as Chief of Staff to the CCB CEO.

My career has been shaped by a progression across public accounting (audit services), investment banking, relationship management and strategic execution. 

•	I began at Ernst & Young serving Media & Entertainment clients in Assurance Services, followed by an investment banking internship at Goldman Sachs. 

•	At Standard Bank, I was a Business Manager to the Global Sector Head for Power & Infrastructure and also spent 5 years as a Relationship Manager for North American corporates operating in Africa.

These experiences shaped my core belief: operational excellence is not just about efficiency — it’s about building scalable frameworks that empower teams and drive growth. 

Throughout my career, I’ve worked at the intersection of business strategy, client coverage, and execution—designing structures, building teams, and fostering cultures that deliver sustainable results. 

I’m passionate about building from the ground up and leading initiatives in high-growth environments that directly impact clients while creating long-term business value.

publications.title: Obesity Related Glomerulopathy in Adolescent Women: The Effect of Body Surface Area
publications.publishedAt: Kidney360, American Society of Nephrology · Jan 27, 2022
publications.description:
Background 
Adolescent obesity, a risk factor for cardiorenal morbidity in adulthood, has reached epidemic proportions. Obesity-related glomerulopathy (ORG) has an early reversible stage of hyperfiltration. Age-appropriate formulae for eGFR, which are standardized to ideal body surface area (BSA) and provide assessment of kidney function in ml/min/1.73 m2, may underestimate prevalence of early ORG. We investigated whether adjusting eGFR to actual BSA more readily identifies early ORG.

Methods 
We studied a cohort of 22,417 young individuals, aged 12–21 years, from a New York metropolitan multi-institutional electronic health records clinical database. eGFR was calculated in two ways: BSA-standardized eGFR, and absolute eGFR. Hyperfiltration was defined above a threshold of 135 ml/min per 1.73 m2 or 135 ml/min, respectively. The prevalence of hyperfiltration according to each formula was assessed in parallel to creatinine clearance.

Results 
Serum creatinine values and hyperfiltration prevalence according to BSA-standardized eGFR were similar, 13%–15%, across body mass index (BMI) groups. The prevalence of hyperfiltration determined by absolute eGFR differed across BMI groups: underweight, 2%; normal weight, 6%; overweight, 17%; and obese, 31%. This trend paralleled the rise in creatinine clearance across BMI groups.

Conclusions 
Absolute eGFR more readily identifies early ORG than the currently used formulae, which are adjusted to a standardized BSA and are not representative of current population BMI measures. Using absolute eGFR in clinical practice and research may improve the ability to identify, intervene, and reverse early ORG, which has great importance with increasing obesity rates.

publications.title: Screening for Obesity Related Renal Damage in Adolescent Women - Body Surface Area Matters
publications.description:
ABSTRACT 
IMPACT: This change will improve primary care physicians and pediatrics ability to identify, intervene and prevent obesity related renal damage in the vulnerable population of young adults.

GOALS: Obesity related glomerulopathy has a reversible stage manifested as hyperfiltration. Early intervention depends on the ability to identify hyperfiltration. Hyperfiltration prevalence is underestimated using the currently recommended formula. We investigated whether calculating BSA-adjusted GFR will more readily identify hyperfiltration. 

METHODS: We extracted data from a large urban, multi-institutional Electronic Health Records (EHR) clinical data research network to construct an EHR data base of 60,549 women and girls ages 12-21 years from the New York metropolitan area. EGFR was calculated in two ways, 1) according to age appropriate formula, and 2) according to age appropriate formula and adjusted to body surface area (BSA). 

RESULTS: Serum creatinine values were similar across different BMI groups. Comparing eGFR values, hyperfiltration rates were similar across BMI groups, ranging between 4%-6.6%. BSA-adjusted GFR was different across BMI groups: hyperfiltration rates were 0.81% for the underweight group, 2.56% for the normal weight, 12.18% for the overweight and 39% in the obese group. This trend of hyperfiltration paralleled the rise in urine creatinine across BMI groups. 

SIGNIFICANCE OF FINDINGS: BSA-adjusted GFR more sensitively detects hyperfiltration due to obesity than does eGFR. Calculating BSA-adjusted GFR will improve primary care and pediatric physicians’ ability to identify, intervene and prevent early ORG. Changes in body composition may account for the increasing discordance between BSA-adjusted and eGFR as BMI rises.

publications.title: An e-Leadership Training Academy for Practicing Clinicians in Primary Care and Public Health Settings
publications.publishedAt: Journal of Clinical and Translational Science · Jan 5, 2021
publications.description: Leadership is an essential competency for clinicians; however, these skills are not a standard part of health professionals’ education and training. Access to resources (time, money) is frequently cited as a barrier for clinicians to participate in leadership development programs. We aimed to tackle this barrier within postgraduate health professions education and training through establishing an online e-Leadership Academy. The e-Leadership Academy was developed as a community–academic partnership between Clinical Directors Network, Inc. (CDN) and the Harvard Medical School Center for Primary Care to train clinicians and healthcare staff in the fundamental concepts and skills for leading within a clinical practice. For this article, the primary outcome analysis examined participants’ responses to both formative and summative evaluations that took place throughout and at the end of the course. Results were used to assess course quality, participant satisfaction, participant engagement, and provide recommendations about future course offerings for a similar audience. The authors propose that future training programs could measure the changes in team behavior and clinical outcomes using expanded evaluations. Proposed plans for expansion of the e-Leadership Academy include developing additional modules, virtual coaching and mentoring, and the potential integration of an in-person component.

publications.title: Using Attendance Data for Social Network Analysis of a Community-Engaged Research Partnership
publications.publishedAt: Journal of Clinical and Translational Science · Dec 1, 2020
publications.description:
Background: The Rockefeller University Center for Clinical Translational Science and Clinical Directors Network fostered a community-academic research partnership involving Community Health Centers clinicians, laboratory scientists, clinical researchers, community, and patient partners. From 2011-2018, the partnership designed and completed Community-Associated Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus Project (CAMP2), an observational study funded by the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, and a Comparative Effectiveness Research Study funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute. We conducted a social network analysis (SNA) to characterize this community-engaged research partnership.

Methods: Projects incorporated principles of Community-Based Participatory Research and PCORI engagement rubrics. Meetings were designed to be highly interactive, facilitate co-learning, share governance and incentivize ongoing engagement. Meeting attendance formed the raw dataset enriched by stakeholder roles and affiliations. We used SNA software (GEPHI) to form networks for four project periods, characterize network attributes (density, degree, centrality, vulnerability) and create sociograms. Polynomial regression models were used to study stakeholder interactions.

Results: Forty-seven progress meetings engaged 141 stakeholders, fulfilling 7 roles, and affiliated with 28 organizations (6 types). Network size, density, and interactions across organizations increased over time. Interactions between Community Members or Recruiters/Community Health Workers and almost every other role increased significantly across CAMP2 (P < 0.005); Community Members’ centrality to the network increased over time.

Conclusions: In a partnership with a highly interactive meeting model, SNA using operational attendance data afforded a view of stakeholder interactions that realized the engagement goals of the partnership.

publications.description: Electronic health records (EHRs) present a research opportunity to provide “rapid assays” for building prospective (historical cohort) studies. However, there are significant challenges to extracting and harmonizing data from different hospital and ambulatory care systems that need to be overcome before EHRs can be readily used to study nutrition-related outcomes. Methods: community-academic partnership with representatives from NYC Community Health Centers (n=4) and Hospitals (n=4), The Rockefeller University, The Sackler Institute for Nutrition Science and Clinical Directors Network (CDN), a primary care practice-based research network (PBRN), was established to build a multisite de-identified database extracted from the EHRs of female adolescents aged 12–21 years and their offspring through 24 months of age, receiving primary care between 2011 and 2015.Representatives convened through 2015 and 2016 to provide guidance on hypothesis development, variable selection, data extraction and review analyses, focusing on nutrition outcomes during pre-conception, prenatal and postnatal periods. Conclusion: the use of EHR is feasible as a rapid assay to describe nutritional outcomes in under-studied populations. Preliminary results appear to confirm the directions and size of associations noted in large observational studies, and will help generate additional hypotheses. Taking a highly collaborative approach with clinicians, IT experts, basic science and clinical researchers has been critical to accomplish data extraction, harmonization’ analysis and quality improvement.

publications.title: Identifying Biologically Implausible Anthropometric Values in a Multisite Extraction of EHR Data for Secondary Use
publications.description: In this multisite study of anthropometric data extracted from EHRs in an urban low resource setting, we quantified the percentage of biologically implausible values to highlight variation in data validity in clinical care. Review of 410,681 records revealed up to 4.31% of values were implausible. Efforts to standardize data checking at time of data entry of heights and weights at point of care could improve data quality.

volunteering.description:
The Grand Central Food Program is under the umbrella of the Coalition for the Homeless. The Grand Central Food Program (GCFP) was founded in 1985 the day after a homeless woman died of starvation in Grand Central Terminal. Since then, the program has grown to become the largest mobile soup kitchen in America.

Each night, our three vans deliver between 800 and 1,200 healthy meals of hot stew, bread, fresh fruit, and juice or milk — as well as coats, hats, gloves and blankets in the colder weather — to those struggling to survive rough on the streets at 25 stops around the city. For many homeless New Yorkers, this is their only meal of the day.  I am honored to be part of a team that delivers food in lower Manhattan on Monday nights.
Delighted to join the Board of the WLC, which works to protect and preserve the open lands. forests, water resources, scenic areas and historic sites in Woodstock and the surrounding area.

headline: Creator of the "How to Dallas" newsletter • AVP at Citi • Loan IQ Operational Readiness
about:
I show you how to enjoy Dallas to the fullest.

How?

Through weekly emails on local news and upcoming events.

Sent every Monday morning.

For free.

Why?

I have bounced around DFW.

2011: Frisco
2021: Little Elm
2022: The Colony
2023: Dallas

After three moves in three years, I found myself feeling disconnected and craving community.

It's hard making friends as an adult.

So I decided to launch a newsletter.

To build the resource I wish I had.

To create a life I love in Dallas.

To help you do the same.

headline: Technology Leader and FinTech Innovator Driving Digital and Process Transformation for an Unfair Competitive Advantage
about: Experienced and knowledgeable Technology Leader skilled in the creation and leadership of high performing teams, application architecture and solutioning and, software development.  Skilled in organizational process and cultural transformation and adoption of new technologies in-line with corporate objectives delivering initiatives and projects that surpass financial objectives.  I bring with me over 18 years of experience leading large projects and cross border teams in multi-national organizations successfully delivering projects in banking and finance and consulting areas.

experience.description:
Lead and manage the engineering team responsible for the Apply and Buy system for Citi Retail Services.  Apply and Buy is the business-critical real-time POS and digital transaction gateway for Citi Retail Services supporting credit card authorizations, credit applications, and transaction settlement, processing over 220 Million USD transactions per day.  

The Integrated Partner Solutions group is a team within Citi Retail Services of the Global Consumer Group of Citibank that caters to retail partners and end customers who require retail private label and co-branded payment solutions.  I lead a team of 37 based in North America, Mexico, and Chennai.  Partner relationships currently supported include Shell, Sunoco, Exxon, Sears, L.L.Bean, Costco, American Airlines, Best Buy, The Home Depot, Macy’s, and Caterpillar.

The Multi-Asset Group Technology team was part of Citibank Global Equities Technology; the team is a front office technology group working with traders and quants in developing and supporting booking, settlement, and confirmation systems.  The project I worked on was the build-out of a system to automate the creation and back-testing of indexes using quant defined strategies.

I was able to reduce rework by over 50% through the use of automated testing and automated builds.  A key contribution that I made was in the transformation of the current software development process from Waterfall to Agile (Scrum) working through the challenges of a distributed team.  As a result, we were able to move into Agile in less than three months after the completion of all Waterfall projects.  Lead and managed the Citi Investment Strategies project Singapore contingent.  My main responsibility includes project planning, stakeholder reporting, timeline management, risk and issue management, team status reporting, requirements analysis, liaise with counterparts in London and North America and design and build the required software solution using Microsoft Technologies and low latency constructs such as parallelism.

The Equity Derivatives Technology Team maintains systems for booking, confirmation, and reconciliation of OTC and listed Equity Derivatives transactions.  These systems include a mix of solutions consisting of vendor software and in-house developed messaging and transport systems using a combination of message standards derived from FPML.   My main responsibility was to design and develop the confirmations system by designing, and implementing the required system features using Microsoft Technologies, the Enterprise Service Bus, and low latency constructs. My biggest contribution was the creation of a trade booking model which allowed specific and graphic communication of trade states through different steps in the booking and confirmation process.  I also directly liaised with other teams to obtain requirements, set management expectations, provide application design, track and manage development work in the implementation of a new system that will be used in place of the existing vendor software to enable straight through trade processing.  

Designed and built a system to report Basel II RWA calculation and capital adequacy requirements for outstanding exposures.  I also built enhancements to the existing Global Regulatory Reporting applications for Basel I reporting to the FSA and other regulatory bodies such as BIS.

RCG-IT is an information technology service provider based in New Jersey, USA running an offshore delivery model with the offshore delivery center based in Manila, Philippines.  I was a member of the Manila offshore delivery center where I was the Application Architect for Microsoft Platform development projects and a member of the strategic architecture initiative group.  As a senior manager my main role was to participate on proposal creation as a member of the pursuit team, manage existing Microsoft projects, and work on the development of technical initiatives to enhance quality and delivery experience and mentor Microsoft developers and future application architects.   

As a member of the senior technology team I was also tasked to work on critical and more complex development projects.  I was able to work on hands-on technology development developing a system to communicate with a GPS portable box and an end user application that can track real-time locations using a GIS package.

Bear Stearns was a Seven-Seven Global client.  I led a team of three software developers under the Microsoft Platform program of Seven-Seven Global.  As the team lead, I provided technical guidance, set sponsor and client expectations; managed project delivery timelines and tracked and escalated issues and risks identified by the project team members. 

I successfully brought a vendor-built solution into an in-house development team for Retail Portfolio Advisor Services at Bear Stearns without any impact to the committed application enhancements and deliveries.  I was also responsible for the build-out of an ASP.Net web application to generate periodic performance reports and sales prospectus materials for the Retail Portfolio Advisory Services Group.  The application was delivered on-time and on-budget with zero re-work and full uptake and end-user satisfaction which translates to the introduction of the capability to generate sales prospectus materials on-the-fly on standard form as required by the legal and sales departments.

Reduced the risk as a new adopter for Microsoft technology by conducting proof-of-concept sessions and working very closely with the business analysis team.  This outcome was on-time delivery of a large, multi-year solution replacing the Accenture.com website.  Led and mentored a cross border team of eight (8) architects between Chicago and Manila and provided architecture leadership for the Accenture.com maintenance and upgrade team at the same time worked on the build-out of the new version of the application.  Delivered a particularly challenging project through constant technology proofs and hands-on work because at the time we were using new Microsoft libraries not yet tested on an application of the same magnitude. The application was built as an ASP.Net web application using Content Management Server 2002 with Commerce Server 2002 as the profiling and targeting system integrated using Microsoft Solutions for internet business. The application was released to production on Nov 2005 at www.accenture.com.   Management responsibilities include issue and risk tracking, stakeholder management, project performance metrics reporting, project charter reviews, time tracking, regular team status reporting, and team performance appraisals.

Prior to building the new application, I was part of the development and operations team that introduced enhancements and maintained the public facing Accenture web application.  I developed and introduced enhancements to the Accenture.com web application using VBSCRIPT, ASP, XML, XSLT, MSXML, ASPEMAIL, COM+, and VB/COM.
Deliver technology training based on the NIIT developed technology curriculum.

publications.title: Impact of the Chicago Earned Income Tax Periodic Payment intervention on food security
publications.description: This article examines the Earned Income Tax Credit Periodic Payment Pilot and its effectiveness in reducing food insecurity for low-income households. Low-income families in Chicago who were eligible for the Earned Income Tax Credit provided data over four waves of data collection between 2014 and 2015. We utilize longitudinal random effects logit models to test the likelihood of experiencing food insecurity. The sample was composed mostly by women with low educational levels. The intervention significantly decreased the likelihood of experiencing food insecurity over time (T2: β = −0.23, p = .581; T3: β = −0.89, p < .10; T4: β = −2.21, p < .01). The Periodic Payment Pilot seems effective at reducing food insecurity in low-income families. Further research should examine how changes to the Earned Income Tax Credit payment distribution could improve the lives of low-income families, specifically concerning food insecurity.

headline: VP, Senior Field Sales Officer
about:
Tom's ability to integrate into any environment and connect with those around him has served his employers well, while at the same time forming the foundational elements of his leadership philosophy. Tom believes in employing a holistic approach to multi-unit sales management which balances the priorities of driving sustainable revenue and profit growth, developing and motivating his sales force, and achieving operational and merchandising excellence, all while maintaining and promoting a customer-centric environment. 

Tom has been recognized by his previous employers for raising the performance standards of his peer group and direct reports. As an accomplished Regional Sales Manager, Tom has been responsible for as many as 196 specialty retail stores in 17 states, with 13 direct reports generating annual sales in excess of $780 million.

experience.description: Tom currently serves as Vice President, Senior Field Sales Officer for Citi Retail Services. Tom collaborates with clients' Territory/Regional Managers to develop and drive private label and co-branded credit awareness, implement credit initiatives, collect and communicate market intelligence, and increase new applications, credit sales and penetration across his assigned territory.

In addition to building and sustaining momentum in existing markets, Tom was successful at restoring newly aligned regions to profitability six times over a nine year period. Collectively, these regions covered nearly 75% of the United States, including Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and St. Thomas in the Virgin Islands, as well as major markets such as Miami, Houston, Dallas, Phoenix, San Diego, Los Angeles, Seattle, Chicago, Detroit, St. Louis, Cleveland, Charlotte and Atlanta. Prior to chain wide downsizing, each newly aligned region increased in unit count and geography, peaking at 196 locations in 17 states, with annual revenue of $980 million.

Tom's proven ability to develop and lead top performing sales teams contributed to his consistent ranking among the top of his peer group in overall KPI performance. As a result, he was twice awarded Regional Manager of the Year. 

Tom's emphasis on the training and development of his team led to four of his District Managers being promoted to Regional Manager and eight Store Managers being promoted to District Manager.

After Camelot Music merged with TWE in April, 1999, Tom focused on acclimating himself to his new company and reestablishing himself as a top performer among his new peer group. In his role as a DM for TWE, Tom had full P&L responsibility for the planning, development, budgeting, operating leadership and staffing of as many as 23 locations in seven states, with annual revenue of $100 million. 

Here too, Tom demonstrated an ability to quickly turn around under-performing stores and excelled at each district realignment he was presented with. Collectively, his portfolio included direct supervision of over 80 stores located in GA, AL, MS, KY, TN, NC, SC. 

During this time, Tom also developed, trained and promoted four Store Managers to District Manager.

Tom consistently ranked among the Top 10 DMs in the company for KPI performance, which led to his promotion to Regional Manager in July 2004.

Tom was promoted to District Manager in March 1995. In this role, he had full P&L responsibility for the planning, development, budgeting, operating leadership and staffing of as many as 22 locations in five states, with annual revenue of $60 million. 

Based in the Atlanta market, Tom's alignment would change annually as he was recognized for his ability to quickly return struggling stores to profitability. Collectively, the number of locations in his portfolio exceeded 60 stores that were located in AL, GA, NC, SC, TN. 

Recognized as a leader among his peer group, Tom consistently ranked among the Top 10 DM's in the company for KPI performance.

During this time, Tom trained and promoted three Store Managers to District Manager.

Tom was promoted to Area Manager in March of 1993, where he managed the daily operations of Camelot Music's corporate flagship store, generating annual revenue of $9 million, while supervising five additional store locations in the greater Canton/Akron market. Collectively, his area generated $25 million in annual revenue. 

Tom's base store delivered a 25% comp sales increase over this two year period, improving the store's ranking for highest company sales from #10 to #3 (out of 400+ stores). He increased annual revenue for his total area by 18%,while reducing shrink by 60%. His base store broke the company's record for highest monthly sales, which he had previously established as a General Manager in Dublin, OH.

During this period, Tom also trained and developed five Store Managers.

After multiple promotions within the Store Manager ranks where he consistently performed among the top of his peer group for overall KPI performance, Tom was one of four Store Managers (out of 400) promoted to GM for Camelot Music's newly formed freestanding division. In this role, Tom managed the daily operations of a 20K s.f. store which generated annual revenue in excess of $19 million and included a full video rental department, an apparel shop and one of the nation's largest classical music departments. 

Included in his scope of responsibility, Tom was given open-to-buy accounts for music, video, apparel and entertainment related gift items. By leveraging these OTB's, refining his inventory mix and aggressively pursuing local marketing opportunities, he increased revenue by 115% over 4 1/2 years and consistently ranked #1 in the company for highest annual sales. Tom also established records for the highest sales in a single day, month and year, while reducing payroll by over $100K in the first year he was at this store. 

During this time, Tom recruited, trained and promoted 16 Store Managers. He also led and /or participated in the set up of 10 new store locations that were in excess of 12K s.f. in size.

Recognized for his merchandising skills, Tom was the recipient of five national vendor merchandising awards.

In March 1993, when Camelot Music developed the Area Manager position to formally train District Managers, Tom was the company's first General Manager to be placed in this position.

headline: Senior Data Scientist at Citi
about:
All data has a story to tell. Behind every number is a person, an entity, or a relationship. Understanding that story tells us how it came to be, what it is doing, or where it is going. Translating data from numbers into a cohesive narrative is the critical successful factor in turning your data deluge into actionable data insights and measurable business impacts. I help craft your data’s story.

I take your data through the analytics continuum to assess what happened through descriptive analytics, ascertain why did it happen by diagnostic analytics, forecast what will happen via predictive analytics, and determine how to make it happen leveraging prescriptive analytics. I discover what makes your data unique and decipher signals from the noise to answer your business questions.

I am technically proficient and am as comfortable using Vim as my editor as much as RStudio or Jupyter Notebooks whether in Ubuntu or Windows. I develop data science insights and solutions using Python and R. I also have experience using SAS. I can apply a variety of modeling techniques from an applied mathematics perspective as easily as I can a statistical or machine learning one. I use the right modeling tools for the job. I am intellectually curious about your data and your questions and will fiercely engage to find your data’s story.

headline:
Dynamic, endlessly curious Marketing Professional who specializes in overcoming Brand/Consumer obstacles.

Integrated Marketing | Brand Strategy | Project Management | Budget Management | Collaboration
topSkills: Marketing Strategy • Brand Management • Project Management • Marketing Communications • Agency Relationship Management
about:
I absolutely believe in learning or doing something new every day and curiosity is my calling card. That makes me valuable as a Marketing problem solver and someone who gets things done.  

I bring over 15 years of experience in integrated marketing across industries as diverse as Finance, Retail, Technology, Automotive, CPG, Travel and QSR.  I drive customer engagement, deliver effective/innovative solutions, create a new go-to-market strategies and make process improvements.

I have a unique perspective on marketing, having worked on both the client and agency sides, and I am known for my ability to bring order to marketing chaos with my strategic and organizational skills.


My core competencies include:
Multi-level integrated marketing | Brand and Product strategy | Project Management | Communications | Media Planning and Buying | Budget administration | Cross-functional Team Building | Collaboration | Agency Management

experience.position: Marketing Program Management Lead Analyst - VP

experience.description:
Managed promotional control systems and offer setup for regular price promotions and loyalty offers. Ensured functionality, allowing for versioning of digital weekly ads and data flows for digital coupon hub. Collaborated with merchant and IT teams on multiple major systems enhancements. Led marketing team of 7.
•	Oversaw daily message management/data flow for in-store shelf-edge signage program with $57M budget, contributing to rollout with third-party vendor supplying shelf tags. Responsible for ensuring all tag templates consistently met brand standards through 3 redesigns.
	Saved ~$9M over 2 years by identifying and resolving data flow issues. 
•	Wrote business cases and collaborated with IT for the implementation of multiple promotional control systems enhancements including capabilities for new price, loyalty and coupon offer types.
•	Initiated a change in how data streams deliver promotional pricing to the POS system going from over 2,500 data streams to 321 streams taking complexity out of the system as well as simplifying the process to do test marketing.
•	Key member of a major initiative to create a mapping of loyalty offer mechanics end to end, resulting in upgrades to IT support/loyalty IT systems and paving the way for the creation of Walgreens Week Loyalty events.  
•	Partnered with Merchandising and Boston Consulting Group to create a seasonal clearance event process to maximize profit by using variable discounting rates by store rather than chain-wide discount rates.
•	Collaborated with supply chain and merchant teams to create a demand shaping program, using targeted promotions by store to work through excess inventory and resulting in $1MM+ incremental profitability/month.
•	Facilitated regular training sessions with merchant team to improve promotional/loyalty offer development and socialize process/systems improvements.

Offered marketing guidance to diverse clients regarding digital and web/social media content development. 
•	Transformed website/sales collateral of software service client from tech-heavy to promotional content, relaying capabilities and benefits of company to prepare for pitches to Microsoft and Amazon.

Key responsibility:  Produced and distributed communications regarding the constant evolution of new Comcast products, product improvements, pricing and sales promotions to ensure all Field Sales personnel in Comcast’s Greater Chicago Region are equipped to provide our customers with the best Video, Internet, Telephony and Home Security services for their particular needs.  

Additional responsibilities included oversight of a budget of nearly $2MM for the region’s collateral, uniform and sales incentive programs.  Direct report team consists of 4 Senior Marketing Specialists.

•	Selected to be one of the first 100 Customer Experience Trainers in the Region.  Participated in weekly Customer Experience Forums conducted by Corporate which are part of a major effort to improve Comcast’s NPS scores.
•	Initiated publication of sales channel specific weekly “Leader Guides” highlighting sales trends, product news, offer news, training topics and HR topics for use by Supervisors in their weekly team huddles.  
•	Redesigned the Regional Sales Incentive programs to more effective metric and ROI based constructs.  This effort resulted in savings of over $100K while still driving desired sales results.
•	Partnered with Finance and IT to create SharePoint tool adopted by all regions that allowed real time ROI reporting and level-appropriate transparency of performance incentives for sales representatives, sales teams leaders and finance leaders.
•	Selected in both 2015 and 2016 to be a Mentor in the Central Region Linked to Leadership program pairing representatives from leadership with promising front-line personnel to develop the next generation of leaders for Comcast.

Managed integrated marketing campaigns for the U.S. and Canada, including brand strategies and $50M in franchisee advertising funds. Oversaw field marketing efforts for Midas and Midas/SpeeDee co-branded shops. Handled creative coordination and oversight of all media planning and buying. Reported directly to CMO. 
•	Drove initiative to automate budget/expenditure reporting across ~9 funding sources, including co-op programs, allowing for transparency at individual franchisee level for ad fund contributions and expenditures.
•	Spearheaded U.S. move from network TV to network radio/digital strategy, contributing to 25% increase in car count and 9 consecutive quarters of comparative sales increases. 
•	Developed Marketing Guidelines for Midas/SpeeDee Oil Change co-branded units including separation of service lists and royalty splits. Worked to open 100+ co-branded units during tenure.
•	Led 5 agency transitions for creative/media functions, including developing list of agencies for consideration and evaluating presentations.
•	Administered Midas brand identity across the enterprise and was responsible for all Marketing related legal clearances.

Reported to SVP in NYC office.  Key member of business development team providing customer and competitive research for new business pitches.   Additionally responsible for leading strategy for the Feld Entertainment account (Ringling Brothers/Disney on Ice) to improve leverage of their barter tactics.

Reported to SVP in NYC.  Responsible for Field Marketing for 25 local Wendy's Franchise Co-ops.  Included sales analysis, message recommendations, media planning/buying and promotional execution.  Supervised 16 team members across 5 different US offices.
Supervision of MTV/VH1 and Starter Athletic apparel media planning and buying.  Supervision of 2 planners.

projects.description:

The objective for this project was to assess and answer related questions on a variety of marketing case studies from around the world including: IKEA, Nintedo and Seiko. 
The IKEA case study related to the sociocultural environment in which IKEA operates. Working on this case study encouraged me to explore the advantages of having the same product range worldwide while respecting the cultural differences in homes around the world. Recommendations were made for IKEA to recognise the different tastes and preferences of each market across the world. I gained a comprehensive understanding of the sociocultural environment and how IKEA had used it within their business to gain customers outside of Sweden.

projects.title: Marketing Policy & Strategy
projects.description:

Piers O' Conor-Nash of Clonalis House, Roscommon offered us the chance to come up with a real life marketing plan with a view to providing him with fresh and innovative ideas. All marketing plans were subject to a 5,000 euro budget. We developed an executable marketing plan for him and presented our findings in a 5,000 word assignment and a 10 minute presentation. Our project included three marketing initiatives that Piers could undertake to boost revenue during the Spring and Summer months. Our marketing initiatives included:
1- A Historical Tour of Ireland aimed at the American and British market.

projects.title: Marketing Research
projects.description:

The main objective of this assignment was to carry out both primary and secondary research to uncover information about the travel industry in Ireland and what affected the decisions to holiday in the country or go abroad.

The initial stage involved gathering secondary information, devising a report and highlighting the reasons for vacations and staycations. The second stage involved gathering primary data. This involved formulating a questionnaire, interviewing various people and composing a highly detailed report illustrating the information discovered. To help us carry out the research we used various databases such as Mintel and OECD.

My knowledge of marketing grew vastly in this Market Research module. I gained a comprehensive understanding of marketing research theory and practice.

about:
I am a senior analyst in the Commercial Bank at Citi, in the Nonprofit Healthcare, Higher Education, and Not-for-Profit sector. I also currently serve on the Analyst & Associate Council, which aims to provide juniors with cross-industry knowledge, exposure to management, and accessible professional development and networking opportunities. Citi Commercial Bank provides comprehensive global banking solutions and industry expertise to mid-sized companies that are looking to grow rapidly and expand internationally. The Nonprofit Team's portfolio includes higher education institutions, hospitals & health systems, international NGOs, cultural institutions, research institutes, foundations, associations, and human services organizations.

I graduated from the University of Chicago in May of 2024, earning a B.A. in Economics with a specialization in Data Science and a minor in Astrophysics. I delivered the Class of 2024's Class Day address, after being selected by a board of my peers and University administration as a student speaker for Convocation. During my time at UChicago, I was a Jeff Metcalf Intern for the University of Chicago's Office of Research and National Labs, where I analyzed and modeled the University's management of two U.S. Department of Energy labs, Argonne and Fermilab. I fostered my passions for food and writing as Editor In Chief for Bite Magazine, the University's premier student-run culinary magazine. I was also a member of the Trott Business Program and The Blue Chips investment group. Additionally, I served as a Resident Dean Assistant for UChicago Housing and Residence Life, a mentor in the UChicago Women's Leadership Program, and a volunteer piano teacher with the South Side Free Music Program.

about:
Jorge Sobehart is a Managing Director, Head of Citi's Credit, Climate and Obligor Risk Analytics, where he develops, implements and manages advanced analytics for wholesale Stress Testing, CCAR/DFAST, CECL and IFRS9, Risk Rating analytics, loss modeling and, previously, Credit Risk Capital. He also manages Climate Risk analytics for physical and transition risk.  

• More than 35 years of experience in advanced Research and Development for government and industry, including over 25 years of experience in Risk Analysis, Quantification of Uncertainty and Probabilistic Risk Assessment in financial services.

• Leader of R&D and quantitative teams, and provider of technical analysis for senior decisions. 

• Experience interacting with domestic and international bank examiners, regulators and auditors.

• Designed and developed Citi’s wholesale methodologies for CECL and IFRS9 Loan Loss Reserves, Credit Risk Capital, Global Systemic Stress Testing, CCAR credit losses for loans, securities and RWA stress testing, market-implied default probability tools and other credit analytics.

• Strong technical background in Model Risk Management and Validation, Financial Engineering, Mathematical Modeling, Probability, Stochastic Systems, Numerical Computation, Time Series Analysis, and Non-Linear Systems. 

• In-demand speaker at domestic and international conferences and training courses in New York, Washington, Boston, Miami, Chicago, Toronto, London, Frankfurt, Paris, Nice, Amsterdam, Geneva, Brussels, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Buenos Aires, Mexico City and many other cities.

• Author of numerous technical articles, book chapters and conference papers in Mathematical Modeling for Credit, Market, Operational and Reputational Risk, Stress Testing and Physics.  Published Science writer. 

• Associate Editor of the Journal of Credit Risk.  Qualified reviewer of technical manuscripts for international journals, book publishers and academic agencies for more than 25 yrs. Member of different professional working groups.

about: Over the past 20 years Graham Buck has developed expertise as a communications professional, writer and journalist who thrives in high-pressure, high-stakes, dynamic environments. He currently works at Citi, where he supports CEO Jane Fraser with her communications and leads teams that cover the bank’s technology and client organizations and create enterprise-wide storytelling campaigns. Buck has previously worked for Mike Bloomberg's presidential campaign, the global strategic communications firm Finsbury and the marketing agency SS+K. He also worked in the Office of the Mayor of New York, where he wrote and developed speeches and other communications for Mayor Bloomberg and launched the office's social media efforts. He played a part in two mayoral campaigns, the 2004 Republican National Convention, and an Olympic bid. Buck began his career as a daily reporter in the Chicago area, covering everything from corrupt school boards to mafia-tinged bedroom communities. Shortly after 9/11, he joined the FDNY, spearheading written communications during the most trying period in the fire department's history. A native New Yorker, Buck is a graduate of Georgetown University and Columbia University's Business School and Graduate School of Journalism. His work has appeared in the New York Times, the New York Post and Reader's Digest among other publications. He has also helped a number of Oscar winners, business leaders and entertainment stars deliver inspirational messages.

publications.title: Consumer Perceptions of Eco-Friendly Products
publications.description: The rate of failure to manage e-waste and the business sectors' failure to produce more eco-friendly products is high. These failure rates cause companies to lose profits on expanding an eco-friendly customer market. The central research question addressed by this correlational design examined the quality, price, and brand loyalty of eco-friendly products related to customers' willingness to recycle e-products. Consumer and buying behavior theories served as the theoretical framework in this investigation. SurveyMonkey was used to distribute the researcher-developed survey to the participants for the collection of the data. The collection data instrument was validated by performing a pilot test using students of the subject organization. The final sample size consisted of 381 participants, 18-24 years old. The strength of the association between ranked variables was determined using Spearman correlation while the customer behavior relationships of interest were examined using ordinal regression. One of the key findings was that when customers had used a certain brand in the past, they were more likely to continue buying that brand, even when the price increased. However, another finding showed that some customers were not willing to recycle electronic devices even if more drop-off recycling facilities were available. The profitability of green product innovations due to brand loyalty, combined with a demonstration of social responsibility by a business, could create a powerful venue for positive social change. The socially-responsible activities of a business could promote awareness that green products and recycling of e-waste are important for an environmentally-secure future.
